justifications.functional_suitability: Core Services Container (Patient Registration, Scheduling Engine with Drools, Billing & Claims) and EMR Service with Audit Trail Interceptor cover R-01 to R-04. Gaps: inconsistent L1/L2 container decomposition, EMR controller described as handling scheduling, and no explicit resource clash mechanism.
justifications.performance_efficiency: Caching Layer (Redis/Dragonfly) in EMR Service, TanStack Query cache in Web Frontend, PgBouncer, Kafka async decoupling and Temporal address the <1s P95 target. Minor gaps: no autoscaling shown, no explicit load targets, and the Query Optimizer is vague.
justifications.compatibility: Integration Worker (Camel) with FHIR Transformer and Connector Client, plus HAPI FHIR adapters, serve lab/imaging FHIR; Insurance Gateway via REST, IdP via OIDC/SAML. Gaps: FHIR logic duplicated across three containers and the SOAP adapter is unclear.
justifications.usability: Web Frontend with Feature Modules serves Patients, Clinicians and Administrators, and Notification Gateway helps. Gaps: no role-specific interfaces, no accessibility, localization or mobile channels, and a patient portal is only mentioned. Usability is largely unaddressed beyond the single web UI.
justifications.reliability: Global Load Balancer (Route 53, Health Check Prober), multi-master Database Layer with Patroni failover, Kafka MirrorMaker 2, DLQ handlers, Temporal and S3 Glacier backups match the 99.99% active-active target. Gaps: contradictory Patroni vs. multi-master design, and no explicit RTO/RPO or per-service redundancy.
justifications.security: IdP MFA, mTLS gRPC, TLS 1.3, KMS with HSM and key rotation, envelope AES-256 encryption, Spring Security RBAC, immutable hash-chained Audit Log Store, Kafka ACLs, and PHI redaction in the Observability Collector explicitly cover HIPAA/GDPR needs, MFA and audit.
justifications.maintainability: Container modularity, database-per-service, Kafka decoupling and fine-grained components are good. Weaknesses: inconsistent L1 vs L2 decomposition, polyglot sprawl (Java, Go, Node, .NET, Python), KMS wired to every container, and duplicated FHIR and audit logic reduce clarity.
justifications.portability: Kubernetes-oriented, hybrid on-prem and eu-central-1 design with Kafka MirrorMaker 2, Vault/AWS KMS dual support, an External KMS Interoperability Adapter and open-source components. Gaps: reliance on AWS Route 53 and S3 Glacier, and no explicit container/IaC deployment definitions.

sensitivity_points: Cache hit ratio for hot patient records
PERF-01.justification: Redis cache, pooling and client caching support sub-second loads, but there is no autoscaling, load model or cache-invalidation mechanism. The 500 concurrent users are plausible but unproven, and the P95 target is only asserted.

sensitivity_points: DB write contention with EMR reads
tradeoffs: Isolation of ingest vs. shared database
PERF-02.justification: Async Kafka decoupling with a DLQ suits the burst, and 10k results in 10 minutes is modest. However, ingestion into the EMR is unclear (the worker doesn't write to EMR), and shared DB contention and read isolation are unaddressed.

sensitivity_points: Replication lag determines potential data loss
DNS TTL and failover detection time
tradeoffs: Async replication vs. zero data loss
AVAIL-01.justification: Geo-DNS, health probes, multi-master and MirrorMaker give a failover path. But asynchronous logical replication cannot guarantee no data loss, conflict resolution is unspecified, and DNS-based failover within 1 minute is questionable.

sensitivity_points: Failover time against the 30 s target
AVAIL-02.justification: Patroni failover and Temporal workflows allow durable retries, but the claims component calls the Insurance Gateway directly. No explicit idempotency or deduplication is shown, and Patroni mixed with BDR is ambiguous.

sensitivity_points: Claims logic embedded in the Core Services monolith
tradeoffs: Monolithic core simplicity vs. change isolation
MOD-01.justification: EMR is separate, so it stays unchanged. But claims are in the Core Services container, which also holds patient and scheduling logic, with a direct gateway call and no pluggable adapter. Changes touch the core service, not one integration component.

sensitivity_points: Audit interceptor capturing the new field automatically
tradeoffs: Automatic AOP auditing vs. explicit field-level audit control
MOD-02.justification: A new field touches the registration component, the UI feature module and the DB schema, with AOP auditing likely automatic, so about three components. But the patient data is split between Core Services and EMR, and there is no schema management approach or data model.

sensitivity_points: Alerting rules and latency for failed logins
SEC-01.justification: IdP with OIDC/SAML MFA and gateway JWT validation deny access without the second factor. However, the IdP is connected only from Core Services, and no component records failed attempts or raises a security alert within 1 minute.

sensitivity_points: Audit coverage of all EMR reads
Policy check for treating-relationship in EMR
tradeoffs: Audit overhead vs. EMR read latency
SEC-02.justification: A hash-chained append-only audit store with an integrity verifier and Glacier archive meets tamper evidence and 10-year retention. But the RBAC enforcer is in Core Services, not the EMR; there is no treating-relationship policy check, and read-audit completeness is not guaranteed.
